hypothesis: Replacing the per-line modulo check with a next-checkpoint counter (1-3% gain) and deferring record-end array pushes until sawMultiline is detected (3-6% gain) should together improve throughput by 4-9% by reducing unnecessary computation for the common case of compact JSONL files where every line is one record.

steps.change: Replace the `line % interval === 0` modulo checks at L271 and L306 with a precomputed next-checkpoint-line counter. After L224, initialize `let nextCp = 0;`. At L271, replace `if (line % interval === 0)` with `if (line === nextCp)`, and inside that block add `nextCp += interval` after the checkpoint push. Do the same replacement at L306 for the EOF path.

Replace the two `number[]` record arrays (L236-237) with lazy storage. Declare `let compactRecordCount = 0;` and `let recordEndOffsetsBuffer = new Float64Array(1024);` after L237 (Float64 because offsets can exceed 2^31). Remove the original `recordEndLines` and `recordEndOffsets` array declarations.

Update the record-closing logic at L275-276 to use lazy storage. Replace the two pushes with: `if (sawMultiline) { recordEndLines.push(line); recordEndOffsets.push(chunkBase + i + 1); } else { if (recordEndOffsetsBuffer.length === compactRecordCount) { const newBuf = new Float64Array(recordEndOffsetsBuffer.length * 2); newBuf.set(recordEndOffsetsBuffer); recordEndOffsetsBuffer = newBuf; } recordEndOffsetsBuffer[compactRecordCount] = chunkBase + i + 1; compactRecordCount++; }`. This keeps only offsets in a growable typed array while the file appears compact.

When sawMultiline transitions from false to true (L279 and L283), materialize the deferred record arrays. Before setting `sawMultiline = true`, add: `if (!sawMultiline) { const recordEndLines: number[] = []; const recordEndOffsets: number[] = []; for (let k = 0; k < compactRecordCount; k++) { recordEndLines.push(k); recordEndOffsets.push(recordEndOffsetsBuffer[k]); } }`. Ensure these arrays are hoisted to function scope so subsequent pushes work correctly.

Update the EOF record-closing logic at L309-310 and L317-318 to use the same lazy-storage pattern as step 3. Also ensure the final array construction at L328-329 handles both cases: if `!sawMultiline`, convert `recordEndOffsetsBuffer.slice(0, compactRecordCount)` to `Array.from()` for both endLines (0..compactRecordCount-1) and endOffsets (from buffer); otherwise use the materialized arrays.

Verify that the hoisting of `recordEndLines` and `recordEndOffsets` to function scope (needed for step 4) does not conflict with their initial lazy-storage state. Move their declarations to the top of the function (after L237) as `let recordEndLines: number[] | undefined; let recordEndOffsets: number[] | undefined;`, and initialize them to `[]` only when sawMultiline first becomes true.

expected_outcome.rationale: The research brief measured that removing all record-end pushes (incorrect output) added about 6% (1.284 -> 1.361). This plan keeps roughly half to two thirds of that gain by deferring the pushes while the file is compact. The nextCp counter removes an integer division on every newline (87,725 per run), adding another 1-3%. Combined, the total should reach 4-9%. The fixture is compact (every line is one record, no empty lines), so the lazy path is exercised throughout the entire benchmark run.

critic_review.rejection_reason: H001: Compound hypothesis. It joins two independent changes, (1) a nextCp counter replacing the modulo check (1-3%) and (2) lazy/deferred record-end storage (3-6%), with separate gain estimates and a combined 4-9% target. Split into separate plans. Non-harness note for the architect: step 4 declares recordEndLines/recordEndOffsets as block-scoped consts inside the if, which shadows the function-scope vars from step 6.
